shy.definition:
n. a quick throw
v. start suddenly, as from fright
v. throw quickly
s. short
shy.translation:
n. 惊跳, 惊避
a. 胆怯的, 畏缩的, 迟疑的, 羞怯的
vi. 惊退, 乱投, 乱掷, 厌恶, 避开
vt. 乱投, 乱掷

shyer.definition:
a. lacking self-confidence
s. short
s. wary and distrustful; disposed to avoid persons or things
shyer.translation: a. 害羞的( shy的比较级 ); 怕羞的; 害怕（做）; <美>缺乏的

shyest.definition:
a. lacking self-confidence
s. short
s. wary and distrustful; disposed to avoid persons or things
shyest.translation: a. 害羞的( shy的最高级 ); 怕羞的; 害怕（做）; <美>缺乏的

shying.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Shy
shying.translation: v. 惊退, 畏缩( shy的现在分词 )

shylock.definition: n. a merciless usurer in a play by Shakespeare
shylock.translation: n. (喻)敲诈勒索的放债者, 冷酷无情的商人, 冷酷无情的人, 夏洛克

shyly.definition: r. in a shy or timid or bashful manner
shyly.translation: adv. 害羞地；羞怯地；胆怯地；小心地

shymkent.translation: 希姆肯特（哈萨克斯坦一城市名）

shyness.definition: n. a feeling of fear of embarrassment

shypod.definition:
When one is hesitant about sharing the contents of his or her iPod.
> Because Doug downloaded Britney Spears' "Toxic" he was totally shyPod when Dru wanted to take a peek at his Library.

shypoo.translation: n. <澳口>劣质酒,出售劣质酒的小酒店

shyster.definition: n. a person (especially a lawyer or politician) who uses unscrupulous or unethical methods
shyster.translation:
n. 讼棍
[法] 奸诈的律师, 讼棍, 不择手段的人

shysters.definition:
plural of shyster

(shyster 的复数) n. 讼棍
